review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

11:1.sourceText: Ἤκουσαν δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ οἱ ὄντες κατὰ τὴν Ἰουδαίαν ὅτι καὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
11:1.targetText: The apostles and brothers throughout Judea soon heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.

groups.note: BSB opens the episode with soon for the connective δέ.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders οἱ ὄντες κατά ("those who were throughout") with the preposition alone.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:2.sourceText: Ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβη Πέτρος εἰς Ἱερουσαλήμ, διεκρίνοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς
11:2.targetText: So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers took issue with him

groups.note: οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς ("those of the circumcision") are the Jewish believers.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies believers; the Greek says only "those of the circumcision".

11:3.sourceText: λέγοντες ὅτι Εἰσῆλθες πρὸς ἄνδρας ἀκροβυστίαν ἔχοντας καὶ συνέφαγες αὐτοῖς.
11:3.targetText: and said, “You visited uncircumcised men and ate with them.”

groups.note: Εἰσῆλθες πρός ("you went in to") is rendered You visited.
ἀκροβυστίαν ἔχοντας ("having foreskin") is rendered uncircumcised.

unmappedSource.reason: Here ὅτι introduces direct speech and has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle λέγοντες to the main verb took issue in 11:2.

11:4.sourceText: ἀρξάμενος δὲ Πέτρος ἐξετίθετο αὐτοῖς καθεξῆς λέγων
11:4.targetText: But Peter began and explained to them the whole sequence of events:

groups.note: καθεξῆς ("in order") is rendered the whole sequence of events.

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγων ("saying") is represented only by the colon before the speech.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀρξάμενος, rendered began, to the main verb explained.

11:5.sourceText: Ἐγὼ ἤμην ἐν πόλει Ἰόππῃ προσευχόμενος, καὶ εἶδον ἐν ἐκστάσει ὅραμα, καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην τέσσαρσιν ἀρχαῖς καθιεμένην ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἦλθεν ἄχρι ἐμοῦ·
11:5.targetText: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision of something like a large sheet being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came right down to me.

groups.note: σκεῦός τι ("a certain object") is rendered something.
ἄχρι ("as far as") is rendered right down to.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB expresses the descent once, with being let down; καταβαῖνον ("coming down") has no separate word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive for the corners of the sheet.

11:6.sourceText: εἰς ἣν ἀτενίσας κατενόουν, καὶ εἶδον τὰ τετράποδα τῆς γῆς καὶ τὰ θηρία καὶ τὰ ἑρπετὰ καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
11:6.targetText: I looked at it closely and saw four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the air.

groups.note: ἀτενίσας κατενόουν ("having gazed, I observed") is rendered I looked closely.
οὐρανός ("sky") is rendered air.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB lists the animals with commas; these καί have no separate word.

11:7.sourceText: ἤκουσα δὲ καὶ φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι Ἀναστάς, Πέτρε, θῦσον καὶ φάγε.
11:7.targetText: Then I heard a voice saying to me, ‘Get up, Peter, kill and eat.’

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

11:8.sourceText: εἶπον δέ Μηδαμῶς, Κύριε, ὅτι κοινὸν ἢ ἀκάθαρτον οὐδέποτε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ στόμα μου.
11:8.targetText: ‘No, Lord,’ I said, ‘for nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’

groups.note: Μηδαμῶς ("by no means") is rendered No.
οὐδέποτε ("never") is rendered nothing … ever, with the negative moved onto the subject.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The preposition εἰς is absorbed by the transitive English entered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:9.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ἐκ δευτέρου φωνὴ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ Ἃ ὁ Θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου.
11:9.targetText: But the voice spoke from heaven a second time, ‘Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.’

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη ("answered") is rendered spoke.
ἐκ δευτέρου ("from a second") is rendered a second time.
The relative Ἅ ("what things") is rendered anything … that.
κοινόω ("make common") is rendered call impure.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The emphatic pronoun σύ ("you") is not separately expressed in this English command.

11:10.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς, καὶ ἀνεσπάσθη πάλιν ἅπαντα εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
11:10.targetText: This happened three times, and everything was drawn back up into heaven.

groups.note: ἐπὶ τρίς ("up to three times") is rendered three times.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:11.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξαυτῆς τρεῖς ἄνδρες ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐν ᾗ ἦμεν, ἀπεσταλμένοι ἀπὸ Καισαρίας πρός με.
11:11.targetText: Just then three men sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.

groups.note: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξαυτῆς ("and behold, at once") is rendered Just then.
ἐν ᾗ ("in which") is rendered where.
ἦμεν ("we were") is rendered I was staying.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

11:12.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ τὸ Πνεῦμά μοι συνελθεῖν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρίναντα. ἦλθον δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ καὶ οἱ ἓξ ἀδελφοὶ οὗτοι, καὶ εἰσήλθομεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀνδρός.
11:12.targetText: The Spirit told me to accompany them without hesitation. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s home.

groups.note: μηδὲν διακρίναντα ("doubting nothing") is rendered without hesitation.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The preposition εἰς is absorbed by the transitive English entered.

11:13.sourceText: ἀπήγγειλεν δὲ ἡμῖν πῶς εἶδεν τὸν ἄγγελον ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ σταθέντα καὶ εἰπόντα· Ἀπόστειλον εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνα τὸν ἐπικαλούμενον Πέτρον,
11:13.targetText: He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.

groups.note: μετάπεμψαι ("summon") is folded into Send … for.
The article with the participle, "the one called", is rendered who is called.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB merges the two commands into Send … for, so this καί has no separate word.

11:14.sourceText: ὃς λαλήσει ῥήματα πρὸς σὲ ἐν οἷς σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ πᾶς ὁ οἶκός σου.
11:14.targetText: He will convey to you a message by which you and all your household will be saved.’

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:15.sourceText: ἐν δὲ τῷ ἄρξασθαί με λαλεῖν ἐπέπεσεν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὥσπερ καὶ ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς ἐν ἀρχῇ.
11:15.targetText: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He had fallen upon us at the beginning.

groups.note: ἐν τῷ with the infinitive ("in my beginning") is rendered As.
BSB repeats the verb in the second clause, where the Greek leaves it understood.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated; As belongs to ἐν τῷ with the infinitive.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated after just as.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject of the repeated verb.

11:16.sourceText: ἐμνήσθην δὲ τοῦ ῥήματος τοῦ Κυρίου, ὡς ἔλεγεν Ἰωάνης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι, ὑμεῖς δὲ βαπτισθήσεσθε ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ.
11:16.targetText: Then I remembered the word of the Lord, as He used to say, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’

groups.note: The imperfect ἔλεγεν ("he was saying") is rendered He used to say.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The μέν … δέ contrast is expressed in English only by but.

11:17.sourceText: εἰ οὖν τὴν ἴσην δωρεὰν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς ὡς καὶ ἡμῖν, πιστεύσασιν ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, ἐγὼ τίς ἤμην δυνατὸς κωλῦσαι τὸν Θεόν;
11:17.targetText: So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to hinder the work of God?”

groups.note: BSB repeats gave in the comparison, where the Greek leaves the verb understood.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB recasts ὡς καί ("as also") as a relative clause, He gave us.
BSB leaves δυνατός ("able") unexpressed; who was I to hinder carries the sense.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the subject of the repeated verb.
English supplies the work of; the Greek says hinder God.

11:18.sourceText: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ταῦτα ἡσύχασαν, καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν Θεὸν λέγοντες Ἄρα καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὁ Θεὸς τὴν μετάνοιαν εἰς ζωὴν ἔδωκεν.
11:18.targetText: When they heard this, their objections were put to rest, and they glorified God, saying, “So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life.”

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσαντες ("having heard") is rendered When they heard.

targetPhrases.text: their objections were put to rest

groups.note: ἡσύχασαν ("they fell silent") is rendered their objections were put to rest.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed; When belongs to the participle.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:19.sourceText: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες ἀπὸ τῆς θλίψεως τῆς γενομένης ἐπὶ Στεφάνῳ διῆλθον ἕως Φοινίκης καὶ Κύπρου καὶ Ἀντιοχείας, μηδενὶ λαλοῦντες τὸν λόγον εἰ μὴ μόνον Ἰουδαίοις.
11:19.targetText: Meanwhile those scattered by the persecution that began with Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the message only to Jews.

groups.note: The article with the participle, "those who had been scattered", is rendered those scattered.
BSB opens the new episode with Meanwhile for οὖν.
The article with the participle, "the one that arose", is rendered that began.
μηδενὶ … εἰ μὴ μόνον ("to no one except only") is rendered only.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle μέν is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB lists the places with a comma; this καί has no separate word.

11:20.sourceText: Ἦσαν δέ τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες Κύπριοι καὶ Κυρηναῖοι, οἵτινες ἐλθόντες εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ἐλάλουν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς Ἕλληνας, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν.
11:20.targetText: But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks as well, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.

groups.note: Κύπριοι ("Cypriots") is rendered from Cyprus.
Κυρηναῖοι ("Cyrenians") is rendered Cyrene, sharing from.
The imperfect ἐλάλουν is rendered as inceptive began speaking.
BSB's Greek text has a different but related word here; Greeks still renders this word.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves Ἦσαν ("there were") unexpressed and makes some of them the subject of went.
BSB turns the relative clause into the main clause, so οἵτινες ("who") has no separate word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐλθόντες, rendered went, to the main verb began speaking.

11:21.sourceText: καὶ ἦν χεὶρ Κυρίου μετ’ αὐτῶν, πολύς τε ἀριθμὸς ὁ πιστεύσας ἐπέστρεψεν ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον.
11:21.targetText: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the [number] that believed", is rendered believed.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins believed, rendering the participle πιστεύσας, to the main verb turned.

11:22.sourceText: Ἠκούσθη δὲ ὁ λόγος εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς οὔσης ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ περὶ αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν Βαρνάβαν ἕως Ἀντιοχείας·
11:22.targetText: When news of this reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, they sent Barnabas to Antioch.

groups.note: Ἠκούσθη … εἰς ("was heard into") is rendered reached.
αὐτῶν ("them") is rendered this.
BSB makes the first of the two καί-joined clauses a When-clause, so the καί between them is rendered When.
BSB follows a reading with an extra word here; to renders ἕως ("as far as").

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed; When renders the καί between the clauses.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders τῆς οὔσης ἐν ("which was in") with the preposition alone.

11:23.sourceText: ὃς παραγενόμενος καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν χάριν τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐχάρη, καὶ παρεκάλει πάντας τῇ προθέσει τῆς καρδίας προσμένειν τῷ Κυρίῳ,
11:23.targetText: When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and encouraged them all to abide in the Lord with all their hearts.

groups.note: The relative ὅς ("who") is rendered he.
πρόθεσις ("purpose, resolve") is rendered with all, expressing wholehearted resolve.
The article τῆς is used as a possessive and rendered their.
BSB's Greek has an extra word here with the same meaning; in N1904 the dative alone gives "in".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:24.sourceText: ὅτι ἦν ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ πλήρης Πνεύματος Ἁγίου καὶ πίστεως. καὶ προσετέθη ὄχλος ἱκανὸς τῷ Κυρίῳ.
11:24.targetText: Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves ὅτι ("for") untranslated.
BSB joins good and full with a comma; this καί has no separate word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.

11:25.sourceText: ἐξῆλθεν δὲ εἰς Ταρσὸν ἀναζητῆσαι Σαῦλον,
11:25.targetText: Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject that the Greek verb ending implies.

11:26.sourceText: καὶ εὑρὼν ἤγαγεν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν. ἐγένετο δὲ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐνιαυτὸν ὅλον συναχθῆναι ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ καὶ διδάξαι ὄχλον ἱκανόν, χρηματίσαι τε πρώτως ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τοὺς μαθητὰς Χριστιανούς.
11:26.targetText: and when he found him, he brought him back to Antioch. So for a full year they met together with the church and taught large numbers of people. The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.

groups.note: The participle εὑρών ("having found") is rendered when he found.
χρηματίσαι ("to be named") is rendered were called.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ἐγένετο ("it came about") unexpressed.
BSB leaves καί ("even") untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves the connective τε untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; the Greek has none.
English supplies the object; the Greek has none.
English adds back, since Barnabas returns to Antioch.

11:27.sourceText: Ἐν ταύταις δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις κατῆλθον ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων προφῆται εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν·
11:27.targetText: In those days some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:28.sourceText: ἀναστὰς δὲ εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν ὀνόματι Ἅγαβος ἐσήμαινεν διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος λιμὸν μεγάλην μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν οἰκουμένην· ἥτις ἐγένετο ἐπὶ Κλαυδίου.
11:28.targetText: One of them named Agabus stood up and predicted through the Spirit that a great famine would sweep across the whole world. (This happened under Claudius.)

groups.note: BSB's Greek has a different form of this verb here, with the same meaning.
ἔσεσθαι ("to be") with ἐπί ("upon") is rendered sweep across; would belongs to μέλλειν.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀναστάς, rendered stood up, to the main verb predicted.
English introduces the reported statement; the Greek uses an infinitive.

11:29.sourceText: τῶν δὲ μαθητῶν καθὼς εὐπορεῖτό τις, ὥρισαν ἕκαστος αὐτῶν εἰς διακονίαν πέμψαι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ ἀδελφοῖς·
11:29.targetText: So the disciples, each according to his ability, decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.

groups.note: εὐπορεῖτο ("had means") is rendered ability.
τις ("anyone") is rendered his.
εἰς διακονίαν ("for a service") is rendered relief.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῶν ("of them") untranslated after each.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:30.sourceText: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησαν ἀποστείλαντες πρὸς τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους διὰ χειρὸς Βαρνάβα καὶ Σαύλου.
11:30.targetText: This they did, sending their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul.

groups.note: διὰ χειρός ("by the hand of") is rendered with.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; the Greek has none.
